task: confirm the retrieval_k=200 candidate-pool effect for commit bug-to-fix search on repositories not used before; issue to its own linked fix, not similar past fixes

selection.order: most recent 5000 non-merge commits at the recorded pin; closed GitHub Issues with nonempty title and body reached by verified direct closing references
selection.eligibility: verified GitHub Issue, CLOSED, nonempty title and body; all linked in-corpus non-merge commits for sampled issue form gold; link labels are not independent bug-fix judgements
selection.shortfalls: report actual numbers, missing issues and search results outside the pinned 5000-commit corpus; never fabricate 200 pairs
selection.merge_policy: merge commits excluded, direct closing refs on merges are not propagated to every branch commit
selection.historical_overlap: none of these repositories appears in any earlier evaluation; Werkzeug and Jinja share maintainers and style with Flask, which stays a caveat

documents.scrub: remove closing-reference phrase spans only; preserve adjacent description; scrub #N, issue/PR URLs, Issue N, Sphinx issue roles and anchors; redact email-like strings
documents.is_fix: message heuristic only in evaluation; assert every gold qualifies independently of links; production may additionally use verified links

split.unit: connected components of issues and gold commit SHAs, within repository
split.tuning: none; all methods prechosen; headline held-out test and separate pooled descriptive rows

models.query_instruction:
Instruct: Given a developer question or a description of behaviour, retrieve the code that implements it
Query:

retrieval.rerank_instruction: Given a bug report, judge whether this commit's changes fix the reported bug

query_budgets.rerank: first 2000 characters, then pair tokenizer max 2048 tokens
query_budgets.interpretation: BM25_2000 is a character-budget sensitivity check, not a matched-token neural comparison

confirm.hypothesis: Building the candidate pool from longer per-signal lists (retrieval_k=200) but still reranking only the fused top 50 raises Hit@5 and MRR@10 for commit search, at no extra reranker cost. Evidence so far is post hoc on the v2 test split (Hit@5 +0.0152 [+0.0037, +0.0309], MRR +0.0113 [-0.0009, +0.0266]).
confirm.scoring: all arms run the production search path with one shared score cache per question: a (query, document) pair is scored once, so arms differ only by which candidates enter the reranked top 50. Arm A is scored again from scratch (no cache) to measure GPU rerun noise.
confirm.primary: B minus A on all fresh questions: Hit@5 and MRR@10, paired evidence-group bootstrap (10,000 samples, seed 42)

rule.noise: |Hit@5(A rerun) - Hit@5(A)| must not exceed the observed B-A Hit@5 effect, otherwise inconclusive
rule.outcomes: keep_50 when a check fails; inconclusive when the checks pass but the interval is wider than max_ci_width_hit5 or the noise check fails; eligible_pending_review otherwise. Nothing changes automatically.
rule.if_adopted: add a per-kind commit setting (retrieval_k is shared by code, docs and commits, and only commits were measured); keep code and docs at 50

timing.arm_order: rotate arm order by question index plus repetition
timing.warmup: one unmeasured production call per arm and repo
timing.label: warm A100 experiment timing, per-repo p50/p95 only; never averaged across repos; not laptop speed

confirm.dev_use: none: every fresh question is evaluation data; split labels are ignored

supporting.note: 66 questions; the nested-50 effect was never examined on dev, so this is a small unbiased check, reported separately

not_measured: similar past fix usefulness for a new bug
